newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway upgrades oil forecast to 3.7 mbpd in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Norway upgrades oil forecast to 3.7 mbpd in 2000.

text.p: Norway said on Wednesday it expected oil production on the Norwegian continental shelf to reach around 3.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2000 and 2001 mainly due to rising output from existing fields.
Previous forecasts estimated Norwegian production to be 3.4 million bpd in 2000, declining to 3.2 million bpd in 2001.
The Energy Ministry said it had upgraded its production estimate for 1998 to 3.5 million bpd from 3.1 million bpd.
According to a Reuter survey of oil companies operating in Norwegian waters, the Scandinavian country pumped 3.1 million bpd in December.
The ministry said it had raised its forecast for total output over the next 10 years by 170 billion cubic metres of oil, or about one billion barrels.
"New technology means that oil companies are now getting more oil from existing fields than earlier was thought possible," said Energy Minister Ranveig Froeiland said in a statement.
"The increase is an example of the quick technological developments talking place in the Norwegian oil industry."

The ministry said the rise in production was attributed mainly to more efficient exploitation of producing fields, as well as an increase in gas sales over the period, as many fields contain both oil and gas.
The higher projections were not based on development of new fields, it said.
It added that increased efficiency and competitiveness in the sector was mainly due to the work of the NORSOK forum.
NORSOK was set up by the ministry in 1993 to identify and assist in initiating measures to improve the competitive standing of the Norwegian offshore sector.
